page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 32 virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2001.0 and high performance in image and text processing. The server demonstrates top-tier capabilities in text generation for small language models, achieving 390.88 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 27932.88 and a Passmark CPU score of 46370.85. Static web serving throughput is strong at 54.65 GB/sec. However, memory performance presents a tradeoff, as the Passmark memory score falls in the bottom 25% despite the large capacity.

The E32s_v6 does not include local storage but is Premium Storage capable, allowing external disk attachments. It does not bundle GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high memory density per dedicated vCPU, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local SSDs. It is well-suited for database operations, memory-cached applications, static web serving, and small-scale language model inference.

The server does not include local storage or GPUs but is Premium Storage capable. Benchmarks reveal strong single-core execution, high-speed static web serving at 54.65 GB/sec, and top-tier text generation for small language models at 390.88 tokens per second. However, memory benchmark scores are relatively weak despite the large capacity. This configuration is highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and web serving.
